shared_elements: low-relief carving on a large stone slab/monolith
photographed in situ in an excavation with soil and rubble around
horizontal band of repeated motifs across the upper part
profile figures (human in A, animals in B)
small rectangular repeated blocks/units used as filler or framing
justification: Both are weathered relief-carved stone monuments shot in the field, each organised as a horizontal band of small repeated units above a zone of profile figures set in stacked registers, which is the most specific correspondence. But the content and manner differ sharply: A is a dense, deeply modelled crowd of elaborately costumed human figures with columns of squared sign-blocks, whereas B is sparse, flat and silhouette-like, with isolated animals and a plain zigzag band on a shaped pillar.
